name: Darién National Park
blurb: Lowland rainforest where figs feed monkeys and harpy eagles hunt sloths.

tip.title: Take away the figs
tip.text: Figs fruit when little else does. Set Fig trees to -100% and watch howlers, bats, toucans and tapirs, then the jaguars and eagles that hunt them.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Darien National Park

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Year-round strong light drives growth in the canopy, while little of it reaches the forest floor.
Wet-season rain keeps the lowland rainforest, swamps and rivers of the Darien green and flooded.
Fallen leaves, fruit and dung build a litter layer that returns nutrients to the roots of forest plants.
Break down dead leaves, wood and animals in the warm, wet litter, returning nutrients to the soil.
Figs fruit through much of the year and are a favoured food of howler monkeys and many fruit-eating birds and bats.

nodes.name: Trumpet trees
nodes.desc: Fast-growing pioneer trees of forest gaps and clearings; their leaves and fruit feed sloths and many other animals.
Stilt-rooted trees that line the tidal coast and shelter the shore, with leaves that some reptiles eat.
A slow tree-dweller that feeds on leaves of forest trees such as Cecropia, and is the main prey of harpy eagles.
A large forest browser eating leaves, shoots and fruit, often at treefalls; only jaguars and large crocodiles can take adults.
Piglike herd animal that eats fruit, seeds, roots and some small animals; jaguars and cougars hunt it.
A large leaf- and fruit-eating lizard of the canopy and riverbanks, itself prey for many birds, snakes and cats.
A big-billed bird that eats mainly fruit, including figs, and so spreads seeds across the forest.
A large pit viper of lowland forest that ambushes rodents, lizards and frogs.
A medium-sized spotted cat that hunts rodents, lizards and other small animals on the forest floor.
The most-recorded bird near the site; it recycles carrion and is recorded feeding on dead iguanas.
The largest cat of the Americas, taking peccaries, tapirs, sloths and other large prey; near-threatened.
A huge forest eagle that takes mostly sloths and monkeys from the canopy; the site holds an important population.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: A wide-ranging cat that hunts peccaries and other mid-sized mammals, sharing the forest with the jaguar.
